transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore, especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork or make household plans together.
When did you first start experiencing this feeling of not being able to settle?
It’s been noticeably worse since I got married and our routines merged—about a year and five months ago.
Did you experience similar difficulties with restlessness or sitting still when you were a child?

Yes. Looking back, it was there in elementary school. My desk was always messy, I’d forget permission slips, and teachers would send notes home because I talked out of turn or couldn’t seem to stay in my seat.
In your daily life now, do you often have trouble keeping your focus on tasks, work, or conversations?
Yes. I can start a planning email or a chapter of a book fine, but within a few minutes I’m staring at the same paragraph and realizing none of it actually went in.
